draft.title: Migration and Australia's cities
card: Many people move to Australia from other countries each year. Most of these migrants settle in the capital cities, not in small towns or the country.
Sydney and Melbourne receive the largest numbers of migrants. They are Australia's two biggest cities.
Cities attract migrants because they have many jobs, schools, hospitals and universities. Many also have communities of people from the migrant's home country, which helps newcomers settle in.
Migrants arriving from overseas add to a city's population. This is a large part of why Sydney and Melbourne keep growing.
draft.remember: Most migrants to Australia settle in capital cities, especially Sydney and Melbourne, and this helps those cities grow.

a.q: Where do most migrants to Australia choose to settle?
opts: In the capital cities, especially Sydney and Melbourne
In small country towns near farming areas
In remote areas in the centre of Australia
In mining towns in the north of the country
a.why: Capital cities offer many jobs, services and communities of people from the migrant's home country. Small towns and remote areas have fewer of these, so far fewer migrants settle there.
a.clue: Think about where jobs, schools and hospitals are found.

b.q: Melbourne's population has grown quickly over many years. How do migrants from overseas help explain this?
opts: Many of them settle in Melbourne and add to its population
Many of them are born in Melbourne and then move overseas
Many of them pass through Melbourne and go to the country
Many of them settle in Melbourne and leave within a year
b.why: Migrants arriving from overseas add people to the cities where they settle, and Melbourne is one of the most popular. The other options suggest migrants do not stay, which would not make the city grow.
b.clue: Growth means more people living in the city.

a.best: In the capital cities, especially Sydney and Melbourne

b.best: Many of them settle in Melbourne and add to its population
